questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to clean your teeth properly
Small everyday changes that help the environment
The history of plastic
How businesses make money from recycling
questions.why: Neil and Sam discuss practical changes people can make, like buying in bulk and passing things on.

questions.q: Why is Neil worried about Sam's toothbrush?
options: She doesn't change it often enough, only once a year
It is too expensive for what it actually does
It is plastic and will last for hundreds of years
It is too hard and damages her teeth and gums
questions.why: He says all her old brushes probably still exist, lasting hundreds of years.

questions.q: How does Sam react to Neil's point about toothbrushes?
options: She strongly disagrees with him and argues back
She says she already uses a wooden brush at home
She thinks it isn't important compared with cars
She's shocked, as she thought she was eco-aware
questions.why: She says she thought she was quite environmentally aware, and 'that's quite shocking'.

questions.q: What does Madeleine Murray find particularly annoying?
options: Multipacks and small packs of products
Big plastic shampoo bottles in hotels
Shops that don't sell rice or pasta loose
People who don't bother to recycle at all
questions.why: She says her pet peeve is multipacks and minipacks.

questions.q: What does Madeleine Murray do instead?
options: She makes her own yoghurt and bread at home
She buys large sizes and fills smaller containers
She only shops at local farmers' markets now
She has stopped buying cereal and snacks entirely
questions.why: She buys in bulk and says we can decant things into lunch boxes.

questions.q: What does Dr Tara Shine suggest new parents do?
options: Buy fewer toys and give them only books instead
Buy only new things for babies, for safety reasons
Pass on things like toys and high chairs to others
Sell their old baby equipment online for cash
questions.why: She says toys, equipment and high chairs can all be passed on.

questions.q: Why are children's things often still in good condition, according to the presenters?
options: Children grow up quickly
Parents rarely use them
They are very expensive
They are made of plastic
questions.why: Neil says children grow up quickly so often everything is in good condition.

questions.q: What does Sam say about hand-me-downs in her own childhood?
options: She never had any, as she was the eldest child
She didn't like wearing them and often complained
Her parents bought everything new from the shops
She got lots from older cousins, which saved money
questions.why: She had lots of toys and clothes from older cousins, which saved a lot of money.
